## Highlights

- Playlist Studio is now substantially more reliable for targeted refinements: you can choose which tracks are editable, lock tracks that must remain untouched, preview the proposed changes and apply them only when the result satisfies the request.
- Prompt constraints are enforced more consistently during both initial generation and refinement, including exact artist counts and recording-version requirements such as live, cover and remix requests.
- Playlist result feedback can now be sent directly to GitHub from a playlist, separately from technical bug reports.

## Playlist Studio

- Added explicit per-track selection and locking so a refinement can affect only the intended part of a draft while protected tracks remain unchanged.
- Improved preview validation so Playlist Studio rejects refinements that do not satisfy requested artist quotas or recording-version constraints instead of presenting them as successful changes.
- Added support for independent exact artist counts and compact multi-artist instructions such as requesting a precise number of tracks from several artists in one sentence.
- Distinguishes between minimum counts, exact final counts and incremental additions, so requests such as “at least 2”, “must have 2” and “add 2” keep their intended meaning.
- Preserves established constraints from the current playlist during later refinements, while avoiding the accidental resurrection of old constraints that a legacy playlist never actually satisfied.
- Improved replenishment behavior when candidate tracks are rejected, reducing unnecessary regeneration and requesting only the missing replacements when possible.

## Prompt and constraint handling

- Added semantic handling for live recordings, covers and remixes across both prompt generation and Playlist Studio.
- Requests such as “only live versions” now validate resolved catalogue tracks instead of relying only on the AI response.
- PlaylistMuse now detects contradictory combinations such as requesting live recordings while **Exclude live tracks** is enabled, shows a clear warning and blocks generation until the conflict is resolved.
- Recording-version intent is interpreted semantically and is not tied to one language or a fixed set of example prompts.
- Added stronger validation for artist quotas after track resolution so the final playlist, not just the AI draft, must satisfy the requested counts.

## Feedback and reliability

- Added **Give feedback** to playlist drafts. It opens a structured GitHub **Playlist result feedback** issue with the original request, refinement context, relevant filters and current track list prefilled.
- Playlist-result feedback is kept separate from technical bug reports and is automatically labeled `playlist feedback`; technical reports continue to use the `bug` label.
- Added a Prompt Quality Memory and regression gate for previously corrected prompt behaviors. Approved cases are exercised in CI so new fixes are checked against earlier fixes before release.

## Interface improvements

- Playlist actions such as Add track, Playlist Studio and Give feedback now use compact icon controls that expand on desktop and remain space-efficient on mobile.
- Mobile playlist action controls are aligned consistently with the desktop toolbar.
- Library pagination is more compact: up to five page numbers are shown on desktop and three on mobile, with dedicated First, Previous, Next and Last navigation controls and accessible tooltips.
- Prompt/filter conflict warnings are positioned consistently with the other generation alerts.
